automation.notes: Inferred: the Color panel's slider mode is display state; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script sets it. The object model has no HSB colour class; scripts convert to RGB themselves.

features.name: RGB (Color panel)
features.summary: Switches the Color panel sliders to RGB.

automation.notes: Inferred: the Color panel's slider mode is display state; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script sets it. A script works with RGBColor values directly instead.

features.name: Web Safe RGB (Color panel)
features.summary: Switches the Color panel sliders to Web Safe RGB.

automation.notes: Inferred: the Color panel's slider mode is display state; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script sets it.

features.name: Color (secondary shortcut)
features.summary: Second shortcut slot that opens the Color panel.

features.name: Enhanced Color Picker
features.summary: Redesigned Color Picker with faster previewing and applying of colours.

automation.notes: Application.showColorPicker opens the Color Picker modally with a starting colour and returns the chosen colour; the picking itself is interactive.

features.name: Color Settings
features.summary: Opens Color Settings to choose working spaces, colour management policies and conversion options.

features.name: Color Themes
features.summary: Panel for browsing Adobe Color themes; removed in later versions.

automation.notes: AiCommandPalette lists it only up to version 25.9.

features.name: Change color tints
features.summary: Adjusting the tint of a global or spot colour.

features.name: Convert color modes
features.summary: Converting colours between RGB, CMYK and grayscale.

automation.notes: Document colour mode switches with the File > Document Color Mode commands (documentColorSpace is read-only); selected art converts with Edit Colors > Convert to Grayscale/CMYK/RGB (Colors7, Colors8, Colors9). Application.convertSampleColor converts individual colour values between spaces.

features.name: Convert to CMYK
features.summary: Converts selected colours to CMYK.

features.name: Convert to Grayscale
features.summary: Converts selected colours to grayscale.

features.name: Convert to RGB
features.summary: Converts selected colours to RGB.

features.name: Duplicate swatches
features.summary: Copying swatches.

automation.notes: No duplicate member; a script adds a new swatch (or Spot) with the same color and a new name.

features.name: Edit colors dialog
features.summary: Editing a colour group in the Edit Colors dialog.

automation.notes: Inferred: the Edit Colors dialog opens from colour-group buttons in panels; no member in any held object-model version, no command id in commands.json and no community script opens or drives it. Colour groups themselves are editable as SwatchGroups.

features.name: Freeform gradient
features.summary: Colours blend between freely placed points or along lines.

automation.notes: Inferred: GradientType has only LINEAR and RADIAL in every held object-model version (2022 to 2025); there is no command id and no community script creates freeform gradients.

features.name: Global process color
features.summary: A process swatch whose edits update every object that uses it.

automation.notes: A global process swatch is a Spot whose colorType is ColorModel.PROCESS; objects take it through a SpotColor whose spot is that Spot, so editing Spot.color updates them all.

features.name: Apply gradients across multiple objects
features.summary: Spreading one gradient across several objects.

automation.notes: Either combine the objects into a compound path and fill it, or give each object a GradientColor whose origin and length span the combined bounds.

features.name: Gradient angle, origin and aspect
features.summary: Direction, start point and ellipse ratio of an applied gradient.

features.name: Gradient annotator
features.summary: On-canvas slider for editing gradient stops, angle and length.

features.name: Dither
features.summary: Adds noise to gradients to reduce banding in output.

automation.notes: Inferred: no member in any held object-model version (Gradient and GradientColor have no dither property), no command id and no community script sets it.

features.name: Gradient
features.summary: A graduated blend of colour stops, linear, radial or freeform.

automation.notes: Gradient.type takes GradientType: LINEAR, RADIAL.

features.name: Gradient
features.summary: Panel for gradient type, stops, angle, aspect ratio and how gradients apply to strokes.

features.name: Perceptual interpolation
features.summary: Blends gradient colours in a perceptual colour space for smoother transitions.

automation.notes: Inferred: no member in any held object-model version (Gradient and GradientColor have no interpolation property), no command id and no community script sets it.

features.name: Gradient presets
features.summary: Ready-made gradient swatches added in Illustrator 30.

automation.notes: The preset names Adobe lists (Water, Wood, Sky, Pastels and others) match the Window > Swatch Libraries > Gradients libraries, which open by command id; applying one from the panel is interactive, or a script assigns it once it is a document swatch.

features.name: Gradient stop
features.summary: A colour, opacity and position along a gradient.

features.name: Gradient swatches
features.summary: Saving gradients as swatches.

automation.notes: Gradients.add creates a named gradient that appears as a gradient swatch; stops are added and coloured through gradientStops.

features.name: New gradient swatches
features.summary: Additional gradient swatch sets added in 30.8.

automation.notes: Unresolved: the 30.8 release says the content libraries gained gradient swatches, but which library files and command ids hold them is not established, and no held object model covers 30.x.

features.name: Gradient Tool
features.summary: Applies and edits gradients directly on objects with the gradient annotator.

automation.notes: Tool id "Adobe Gradient Vector Tool" (AiCommandPalette tool list) activates the tool; dragging the annotator stays interactive. A script sets the same placement on a GradientColor's origin, angle and length.

features.name: Grayscale color
features.summary: Colour defined by a single tint of black.

features.name: Group swatches
features.summary: Organising swatches into groups.

automation.notes: Create a group with SwatchGroups.add and name it; put swatches in with addSwatch and spot or global colours with addSpot.

features.name: Invert Colors
features.summary: Inverts the colours of the selection.

features.name: Lab color
features.summary: Device-independent colour defined by lightness and a and b axes.

features.name: Precise spot colors using Lab values
features.summary: Displaying and outputting spot colours from their Lab definitions.

automation.notes: A spot defined from Lab values has spotKind SpotColorKind.SPOTLAB with a LabColor as its color. The Swatches panel's Spot Colors option (use Lab or book CMYK values for display and output) has no member or command.

features.name: Linear gradient
features.summary: Colours blend along a straight line.

automation.notes: Gradient.type takes GradientType: LINEAR, RADIAL.

features.name: Move colors into groups
features.summary: Moving swatches into swatch groups.

automation.notes: addSwatch or addSpot moves an existing swatch into the target swatch group.

features.name: Move from library
features.summary: Adding swatches from a library to the document.

automation.notes: Dragging from a library panel is interactive. A script opens the library .ai file as a document, reads its swatches and recreates them in the target document (the transferSwatches community script does this between documents).

features.name: New Swatch
features.summary: Creates a swatch from the current colour.

features.name: None
features.summary: Absence of fill or stroke.

automation.notes: Assign a NoColor object (new NoColor()) to fillColor or strokeColor, or set filled/stroked to false. NoColor has no members of its own.

features.name: Overprint Black
features.summary: Sets black in the selection to overprint, optionally including rich blacks.

features.name: Apply a predefined gradient
features.summary: Applying a gradient swatch.

automation.notes: Assign a gradient swatch's color (a GradientColor) to fillColor or strokeColor. Gradients in a library must first be in the document (see Move from library).

features.name: Process swatches
features.summary: Creating process colour swatches, optionally global.

automation.notes: Plain process swatch: Swatches.add with a CMYKColor or RGBColor. Global process swatch: Spots.add with colorType ColorModel.PROCESS.

features.name: Proof Colors
features.summary: Turns soft-proofing on or off using the current proof setup.

features.name: Customize
features.summary: Defines a custom proof condition from a device profile.

automation.notes: View > Proof Setup > Customize (command 'proof-custom') opens the Customize Proof Condition modal dialog, and no object-model member sets a proof condition or device profile. The preset proof setups are reachable (set_color_view).

features.name: Color blindness - Deuteranopia-type
features.summary: Simulates how artwork looks to people with deuteranopia-type colour blindness.

features.name: Legacy Macintosh RGB (Gamma 1.8)
features.summary: Soft-proofs colours as they appear on a legacy Mac RGB (gamma 1.8) display.

features.name: Monitor RGB
features.summary: Soft-proofs colours using the monitor's own profile.

features.name: Color blindness - Protanopia-type
features.summary: Simulates how artwork looks to people with protanopia-type colour blindness.

features.name: Internet Standard RGB (sRGB)
features.summary: Soft-proofs colours as they appear in sRGB.

features.name: Working CMYK
features.summary: Soft-proofs colours as they will print in the working CMYK space.

features.name: Radial gradient
features.summary: Colours blend outward from a centre.

automation.notes: Gradient.type takes GradientType: LINEAR, RADIAL.

features.name: Recolor add remove
features.summary: Adding or removing colours from colour groups.

automation.notes: Colour groups are SwatchGroups; a script adds colours with addSwatch/addSpot and removes them with Swatch.remove. Doing it inside the Recolor Artwork dialog is interactive.

features.name: Assign
features.summary: Tab for mapping current colours to new colours.

automation.notes: Inferred: a tab of the Recolor Artwork dialog; no member in any held object-model version, no command id that sets it and no community script reaches it. The dialog opens with Recolor Art Dialog.

features.name: Current Colors
features.summary: Original colours found in the artwork.

automation.notes: Inferred: a column of the Recolor Artwork dialog; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script reaches it. A script can list the colours in use only by walking the artwork.

features.name: Edit
features.summary: Tab for editing colours on a wheel or with sliders.

automation.notes: Inferred: a tab of the Recolor Artwork dialog; no member in any held object-model version, no command id that sets it and no community script reaches it.

features.name: Exclude selected colors so they will not be recolored
features.summary: Protects chosen colours from recolouring.

automation.notes: Inferred: a control inside Recolor Artwork; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script reaches it.

features.name: Harmony Rules
features.summary: Generates a group from a base colour.

automation.notes: Inferred: a control inside Recolor Artwork; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script reaches it.

features.name: Merge colors into a row
features.summary: Maps several current colours to one new colour.

automation.notes: Inferred: a control inside Recolor Artwork; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script reaches it.

features.name: New Row
features.summary: Adds a row for a manual mapping.

automation.notes: Inferred: a control inside Recolor Artwork; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script reaches it.

features.name: Preset
features.summary: Recolour presets such as one colour job or colour library.

automation.notes: Edit > Edit Colors > Recolor with Preset items (Color library, Single, Two, Three Color, Color Harmony) open Recolor Artwork with that preset; needs selected artwork and the dialog stays interactive. Edit > Edit Colors > Recolor with Preset items ('_GenericPluginMenuItem 62' to '66') open a library picker and then the Recolor Artwork modal dialog with the preset loaded; the result must be confirmed by the user. No object-model member applies a recolour preset.

features.name: Recolor Art
features.summary: Applies the changes to the selected artwork.

automation.notes: Inferred: a checkbox inside Recolor Artwork; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script reaches it.

features.name: Separate colors into different rows
features.summary: Splits merged colours back out.

automation.notes: Inferred: a control inside Recolor Artwork; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script reaches it.

features.name: Recolor Artwork
features.summary: Opens Recolor Artwork to reassign, reduce or harmonise the colours of selected artwork.

automation.notes: Edit > Edit Colors > Recolor Artwork (command 'Recolor Art Dialog') opens the Recolor Artwork modal dialog; reassigning, reducing and harmonising colours happen inside it and no object-model member or published Action parameters drive it. Individual adjustments it offers are scriptable separately (adjust_colors, edit_swatch_group).

features.name: Recolor assign
features.summary: Assigning new colours to selected artwork.

automation.notes: Inferred: the Assign mapping exists only inside Recolor Artwork; no member in any held object-model version, no command id that performs it and no community script drives it. Scripts recolour by setting fillColor/strokeColor on each object instead.

features.name: Recolor change group
features.summary: Changing colours inside a colour group.

automation.notes: Changing the colours of a colour group outside the dialog: read the group's swatches and set their color (for global or spot colours, Spot.color, which updates art using them).

features.name: Recolor color reduction
features.summary: Reducing the number of colours with tints, shades and presets.

automation.notes: Recolor with Preset > Single, Two or Three Color opens Recolor Artwork set to reduce colours; needs selected artwork and the dialog must be confirmed by the user. A plug-in can reduce colours without the dialog through AIColorHarmonySuite.ReduceNumberOfColors. Colour reduction (Recolor with Preset > Single, Two or Three Color, '_GenericPluginMenuItem 63' to '65') opens the Recolor Artwork modal dialog. Its reduction algorithm (tints and shades mapped to a colour group) is only exposed to C++ plug-ins (AIColorHarmonySuite.ReduceNumberOfColors), not to ExtendScript, so a script cannot reproduce it faithfully.

features.name: Recolor delete groups
features.summary: Deleting colour groups.

automation.notes: SwatchGroup.remove deletes a colour group.

features.name: Recolor edit individual
features.summary: Editing one colour inside a group.

automation.notes: Outside the dialog a script edits one colour of a group by setting that swatch's color; inside Recolor Artwork it is interactive.

features.name: Recolor limit
features.summary: Limiting artwork to the colours of a library.

automation.notes: Recolor with Preset > Color library opens Recolor Artwork limited to a chosen library; needs selected artwork and the choice and confirmation are interactive. Limiting artwork to a library's colours (Recolor with Preset > Color library, '_GenericPluginMenuItem 62') opens a library picker and the Recolor Artwork modal dialog; the colour assignment it performs has no object-model member or published Action parameters.

features.name: Recolor local global
features.summary: Changing one colour or all colours together.

automation.notes: Inferred: linked versus independent editing exists only inside Recolor Artwork; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script reaches it.

features.name: Advanced Options
features.summary: Opens the full Recolor Artwork dialog.

automation.notes: Edit > Edit Colors > Recolor Artwork opens the full dialog; needs selected artwork, and everything in the dialog is then interactive. Advanced Options is the full Recolor Artwork modal dialog (command 'Recolor Art Dialog'); every setting in it is interactive and has no object-model member or published Action parameters.

features.name: Change color order randomly
features.summary: Shuffles colour assignments.

automation.notes: Inferred: a button inside Recolor Artwork; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script reaches it. Scripts that randomise colours (for example RandomColorFromSwatches) do so by assigning fillColor themselves.

features.name: Change saturation and brightness randomly

features.name: Color Library

features.name: Color Theme Picker

features.name: Color wheel

automation.notes: Inferred: on-screen wheel inside Recolor Artwork; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script reaches it.

features.name: Colors

automation.notes: AIColorHarmonySuite.ReduceNumberOfColors (2025 SDK) reduces an art object to a given number of colours without the dialog. Scripts can only open Recolor Artwork (Recolor Art Dialog) and leave the count to the user.

features.name: Link Unlink harmony colors

features.name: Color library

automation.notes: Edit > Edit Colors > Recolor with Preset > Color library ('_GenericPluginMenuItem 62') opens a library picker and then the Recolor Artwork modal dialog; nothing completes it unattended.

features.name: Add Used Colors
features.summary: Adds every colour used in the artwork as swatches.

automation.notes: No command id. A script emulates it by collecting the fill and stroke colours of the artwork and adding a swatch for each one not already present.

features.summary: Removes the selected swatch or group.

automation.notes: No command id; a script duplicates by adding a swatch with the same color and a new name. For a global or spot swatch, add a Spot with the same color and colorType (Spots.add).

automation.notes: Inferred: panel view option; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script sets it.

features.name: Merge Swatches
features.summary: Combines selected swatches into the first one selected.

automation.notes: Inferred: no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script merges swatches. A script can only emulate it by reassigning the colour of every object that uses the other swatches and then calling Swatch.remove.

features.name: New Swatch Group
features.summary: Creates an empty swatch group or one from the selected swatches.

features.name: Open Swatch Library
features.summary: Opens a swatch library panel.

automation.notes: Each built-in library has its own Window > Swatch Libraries command id in commands.json ("_Swatch Library Menu Item <n>"); Other Library opens a file dialog. Opening only shows the library panel; its swatches enter the document when used.

features.name: Save Swatch Library as AI
features.summary: Saves swatches as an Illustrator library file.

automation.notes: No command id for the panel item. An Illustrator document holding the swatches, saved with Document.saveAs, can be opened as a library with Other Library; this approximates the panel item rather than invoking it.

features.name: Save Swatch Library as ASE
features.summary: Saves swatches in the Adobe Swatch Exchange format for other apps.

automation.notes: Inferred: no member in any held object-model version writes Adobe Swatch Exchange files, there is no command id and no community script in the corpus does it.

features.name: Select All Unused
features.summary: Selects swatches no object uses.

automation.notes: Only in the Swatches panel menu, which executeMenuCommand cannot reach. features.name: Show Find Field

automation.notes: Inferred: panel display option; no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script toggles it. Swatches.getByName finds a swatch by name instead.

features.name: Sort By Kind

automation.notes: The Color panel's out-of-gamut and web-safe warnings are not exposed. A script can bring a colour into the CMYK gamut by converting it with Application.convertSampleColor, or make RGB web safe by rounding each component to a multiple of 51.

domains.name: Typography
domains.covers: Type objects and text formatting: type tools, fonts, character and paragraph settings, styles, glyphs, spelling and Asian type.

features.name: Adobe Fonts
features.summary: Browsing and activating fonts from Adobe Fonts without leaving Illustrator.

automation.notes: Type > More from Adobe Fonts opens browsing; activating fonts is done by the user. TextFonts.isFontAvailable checks whether a font is present. Activating Adobe Fonts happens in Adobe Fonts or the Creative Cloud app, reached through Browse Typekit Fonts Menu IllustratorUI. A script can only check whether a font is present (TextFonts.isFontAvailable, used by list_document_fonts) and replace it (replace_font).

automation.notes: ParagraphAttributes.justification takes Justification: CENTER, FULLJUSTIFY, FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINECENTER, FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINELEFT, FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINERIGHT, LEFT, RIGHT.

features.name: Left Align Text

automation.notes: ParagraphAttributes.justification takes Justification: CENTER, FULLJUSTIFY, FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINECENTER, FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINELEFT, FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINERIGHT, LEFT, RIGHT.

features.name: Right Align Text

automation.notes: justification takes Justification: LEFT, CENTER, RIGHT, FULLJUSTIFY, FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINELEFT, FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINECENTER, FULLJUSTIFYLASTLINERIGHT.

features.name: Replace characters with alternate glyphs
features.summary: Swapping characters for alternates from the Glyphs panel or on-canvas widget.

automation.notes: A glyph with its own Unicode value is written into contents; alternateGlyphs picks a width or form variant (AlternateGlyphsForm). Alternates without a Unicode value can only be chosen in the Glyphs panel or on-canvas widget. Only whole features reach text: CharacterAttributes.alternateGlyphs (Asian alternate forms such as JIS or width variants), stylisticAlternates, swash and titling, all set by set_character_attributes. Replacing one character with a specific alternate from the Glyphs panel or the on-canvas alternates widget has no object-model member.

automation.notes: TextFrame.antialias takes TextAntialias: CRISP, NONE, SHARP, STRONG.

automation.notes: Type > Area Type Options opens a modal dialog that includes Auto Size, set by the user; no member exposes it. Needs a selected area type object. Auto Size is set only in Type > Area Type Options ('area-type-options'), which opens a modal dialog, or with the on-canvas widget; no TextFrame member exposes it, and no Action parameters for it are published. Scripts can resize the type area once through TextFrame.textPath.height (set_text_frame_options height), but cannot turn Auto Size on.

features.name: Dynamic symbol
features.summary: Symbol type whose instances can keep local appearance changes while sharing shape edits.

automation.notes: Symbols.add takes only source art and a registration point, and Symbol has no type property in any held object-model version. The type is chosen in the New Symbol dialog (Adobe New Symbol Shortcut, needs selected art) or in Symbol Options. The symbol type (Dynamic Symbol) is chosen only in the New Symbol dialog (Symbols panel > New Symbol..., menu command Adobe New Symbol Shortcut) or Symbol Options, both modal. automation.notes: Edit > Edit Original (EditOriginal Menu Item) opens the selected linked file in another application (for example Photoshop), and the editing happens there by hand. Illustrator gets no signal when the edit ends, so nothing unattended completes the feature; the server does not offer it. After the file is saved elsewhere, update_links reloads it.

features.name: Embed images

features.name: Place linked Photoshop documents

automation.notes: A placed item with file set to the PSD stays linked; editing in Photoshop is outside Illustrator.

features.name: Edit Original
features.summary: Opens the linked file in its source application.

automation.notes: Edit > Edit Original; needs a selected linked item and opens the source application. The Links panel's Edit Original runs the same command (EditOriginal Menu Item): it opens the linked file in its source application for manual editing, so it cannot complete unattended. update_links reloads the file once it has been saved.

automation.notes: Inferred: no member in any held object-model version (2022-2025), no command id in commands.json and no community script in the corpus reaches it. The library browser is interactive; relinking to a local file is possible with PlacedItem.relink.

features.name: Update Link
features.summary: Reloads a changed linked file.

automation.notes: The Links panel command needs the link selected in the panel; relinking a placed item to its own file with PlacedItem.relink also reloads it.

features.name: Embed Image
features.summary: Embeds the linked file's content in the document.

features.name: Links

No object-model member adjusts art inside a mockup, so running the command unattended leaves Illustrator in an editing state with nothing to finish it. Not offered; run_image_command makes and releases mockups.

features.name: Make / Preview

features.name: Mockup

features.name: Release

features.name: Save mockups as templates

automation.notes: Object > Create Object Mosaic... (AI Object Mosaic Plug-in4) opens a modal dialog. No object-model member makes a mosaic, and ExtendScript cannot read a raster item's pixel colours, so it cannot be rebuilt from tiles the way the dialog describes. No published Action parameters for it were found.

features.name: Photoshop Import Options

features.name: Move part of an image from Photoshop

automation.notes: Pasting a copied Photoshop selection from the clipboard; the copy happens in Photoshop. The copy happens in Photoshop. The Illustrator half is Application.paste (or Edit > Paste through execute_menu_command), but a script cannot tell what the clipboard holds: pixels paste directly, while Photoshop paths open the Paste Options dialog. No tool offers a blind paste.

features.name: Move paths from Photoshop
features.summary: Bringing Photoshop paths into Illustrator.

automation.notes: Paths exported from Photoshop as an Illustrator file are opened with Application.open, or pasted from the clipboard with Application.paste; the Photoshop side needs Photoshop scripting. Only the Illustrator half is scriptable here. Paths exported from Photoshop with File > Export > Paths to Illustrator are an .ai file that Application.open (open_document) opens. The export itself needs Photoshop. Pasting a copied Photoshop path opens the Paste Options dialog (Compound Shape or Compound Path), so the clipboard route is not unattended.

automation.notes: Trace the image (PlacedItem.trace or RasterItem.trace), then load this built-in preset into the result's tracingOptions with loadFromPreset, using the preset name exactly as Application.tracingPresetsList returns it (the exact string is not recorded here). features.name: Release
features.summary: Discards the tracing and keeps the original image.

features.name: Create a text poster using Image Trace
features.summary: Tutorial combining Image Trace with type.

automation.notes: Tutorial steps (trace an image, expand it, set type inside or over the shapes) are each scriptable; the design choices are the user's.

features.name: Image Trace object
features.summary: A live tracing that keeps the source image and the traced vector result until it is expanded.

features.name: Tracing Presets
features.summary: Manages saved Image Trace presets.

automation.notes: Edit > Tracing Presets... (menu command TracingPresets) opens a modal dialog, so it cannot run unattended. Only part of what it does has an object-model route: Application.tracingPresetsList lists presets and TracingOptions.storeToPreset creates or overwrites an unlocked one (list_tracing_presets, set_trace_options savePreset). Deleting, renaming, importing and exporting presets have no member.

domains.name: Meshes
domains.covers: Gradient mesh objects and the tools and commands that create and edit them.

features.name: Create Gradient Mesh
features.summary: Converts the selection into a regular gradient mesh with set rows, columns and highlight.

automation.notes: Object > Create Gradient Mesh (make mesh) opens a modal dialog. No object-model member creates a mesh (MeshItems has no add) and no published script or Action records the event (searched GitHub); a plug-in uses AIMeshSuite.

features.name: Edit mesh objects
features.summary: Adding, moving and recolouring mesh points and patches.

automation.notes: Adding lines, moving points and recolouring patches is done with AIMeshSuite and the vertex, segment and patch iterator suites (InsertU/InsertV, SetPoint, SetColor). Scripts cannot create or edit mesh points; they can only duplicate or move whole mesh items.

features.name: Convert a gradient-filled object to a mesh
features.summary: Expanding a gradient fill into a gradient mesh.

automation.notes: Object > Expand (Expand3) opens the Expand dialog, where Gradient Mesh is chosen for the gradient fill; needs a selection and the dialog is interactive. No member converts gradients to meshes. Object > Expand (Expand3) opens the modal Expand dialog. Published actions record its event, ai_plugin_expand, with booleans 'objt', 'fill', 'strk' and a fourth, 'smth' (1936553064), which AI_PS_Library calls gradient; no source establishes that it selects Expand Gradient To: Gradient Mesh rather than Specify Objects, or how the object count is carried, so it is not used. Recording Object > Expand with Gradient Mesh chosen would establish it.

features.name: Gradient mesh
features.summary: An object divided by mesh lines into patches whose points each carry a colour that blends smoothly.

automation.notes: MeshItem exposes no mesh-specific members; points and colours are not scriptable.

features.name: Appearance
features.summary: Highlight style: flat, to centre or to edge.

automation.notes: Flat, To Center or To Edge is chosen in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog opened by make mesh on the selection; no object-model member. Set in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog that Object > Create Gradient Mesh (make mesh) opens modally on the selection. MeshItem has no members in the 2022-2025 object models, and no published script or Action records the event (searched GitHub); a plug-in sets this through AIMeshSuite.

features.name: Columns
features.summary: Number of vertical mesh lines.

automation.notes: Set in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog that make mesh opens on the selection; MeshItem has no member for it. A plug-in sets grid size with AIMeshSuite.InitCartesian. Set in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog that Object > Create Gradient Mesh (make mesh) opens modally on the selection. MeshItem has no members in the 2022-2025 object models, and no published script or Action records the event (searched GitHub); a plug-in sets this through AIMeshSuite.

features.name: Highlight
features.summary: Strength of the white highlight.

automation.notes: Set in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog opened by make mesh on the selection; no object-model member. Set in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog that Object > Create Gradient Mesh (make mesh) opens modally on the selection. MeshItem has no members in the 2022-2025 object models, and no published script or Action records the event (searched GitHub); a plug-in sets this through AIMeshSuite.

features.name: Rows
features.summary: Number of horizontal mesh lines.

automation.notes: Set in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog that make mesh opens on the selection; MeshItem has no member for it. A plug-in sets grid size with AIMeshSuite.InitCartesian. Set in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog that Object > Create Gradient Mesh (make mesh) opens modally on the selection. MeshItem has no members in the 2022-2025 object models, and no published script or Action records the event (searched GitHub); a plug-in sets this through AIMeshSuite.

features.name: To Center
features.summary: Places a highlight in the centre of the object.

automation.notes: An Appearance choice in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog opened by make mesh on the selection; no object-model member. Set in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog that Object > Create Gradient Mesh (make mesh) opens modally on the selection. MeshItem has no members in the 2022-2025 object models, and no published script or Action records the event (searched GitHub); a plug-in sets this through AIMeshSuite.

features.name: To Edge
features.summary: Places a highlight at the edges of the object.

automation.notes: An Appearance choice in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog opened by make mesh on the selection; no object-model member. Set in the Create Gradient Mesh dialog that Object > Create Gradient Mesh (make mesh) opens modally on the selection. MeshItem has no members in the 2022-2025 object models, and no published script or Action records the event (searched GitHub); a plug-in sets this through AIMeshSuite.

features.name: Convert mesh objects to paths
features.summary: Recovering the outline path of a mesh object.

automation.notes: Object > Path > Offset Path (OffsetPath v23) with an offset of 0 on a selected mesh yields its outline path; the command opens the Offset Path dialog. Object > Path > Offset Path (OffsetPath v23) with an offset of 0 opens the modal Offset Path dialog. MeshItem exposes no geometry, and no source shows that the Offset Path LiveEffect applied with PageItem.applyEffect to a mesh yields its outline, so no unattended route is established.

features.name: Mesh Tool
features.summary: Adds mesh points and lines to an object and edits their colours and handles.

automation.notes: Tool id "Adobe Mesh Editing Tool" (AiCommandPalette tool list) activates the tool; clicking to add mesh points stays interactive. Object > Create Gradient Mesh (make mesh) builds a regular mesh from a selection through its dialog; mesh points are editable only through the C++ SDK (AIMeshSuite).

features.name: Transparency in gradient meshes
features.summary: Opacity values on individual mesh points.

automation.notes: Per-point opacity is set with AIMeshVertexIteratorSuite.SetOpacity in the C++ SDK (AIMesh.h). MeshItem exposes no mesh points in any held object-model version, and community answers confirm points are out of reach of scripts.

domains.name: Blends
domains.covers: Blend objects that interpolate shape and color between objects, and their options and spines.

features.name: Expand
features.summary: Turns the blend steps into separate objects.

features.name: Make
features.summary: Blends the selected objects.

features.name: Blend
features.summary: Live object that generates intermediate shapes and colours between two or more objects along a spine.

automation.notes: A script creates, releases or expands a blend only through these menu commands on the current selection (two or more objects for Make). In the object model a blend is a generic PluginItem with no blend-specific properties, so steps, spine and options cannot be read or set there.

features.name: Align to Page
features.summary: Keeps steps upright relative to the page.

automation.notes: Orientation value 0 (key 'rota') in a loaded ai_plugin_liveblend action event, played on a selected blend with app.doScript.

features.name: Align to Path
features.summary: Rotates steps to follow the spine.

automation.notes: Orientation value 1 (key 'rota') in a loaded ai_plugin_liveblend action event, played on a selected blend with app.doScript.

features.name: Orientation
features.summary: Whether steps align to the page or to the path.

automation.notes: Enumerated parameter key 'rota' of the ai_plugin_liveblend action event: 0 Align to Page, 1 Align to Path. Applied by app.loadAction plus app.doScript with a blend selected; no object-model member.

features.name: Smooth Color
features.summary: Automatic step count for smooth colour.

automation.notes: A choice of the spacing enum in the recordable Blend Options event (ai_plugin_liveblend), applied by loading and playing an action on a selected blend. Its enum value is not evidenced; record the action to obtain it. No object-model member exposes it. The recordable Blend Options event (ai_plugin_liveblend) carries spacing as the enumerated 'menu' parameter (key 1835363957), but only Specified Steps (value 5) is evidenced. No published script or recorded action gives the 'menu' value for Smooth Color (checked BlendSp, AI_PS_Library and public .aia files on GitHub). Record Object > Blend > Blend Options with this spacing in Illustrator to obtain them; no object-model member exposes it.

features.name: Spacing
features.summary: How steps are calculated: smooth colour, specified steps or specified distance.

automation.notes: No object-model member or direct command sets it; Path Blend Options only opens the dialog. Community scripts load a generated action whose event ai_plugin_liveblend carries the spacing as an enumerated parameter (key 'menu'), then run it with app.loadAction/app.doScript on a selected blend. Only the value used for Specified Steps (5) is evidenced.

features.name: Specified Distance
features.summary: Exact distance between steps.

automation.notes: Part of the recordable Blend Options event (ai_plugin_liveblend), applied by loading and playing an action on a selected blend. The enum value and parameter key for the distance are not evidenced; record the action in Illustrator to get them. No object-model member exposes it. The recordable Blend Options event (ai_plugin_liveblend) carries spacing as the enumerated 'menu' parameter (key 1835363957), but only Specified Steps (value 5) is evidenced. No published script or recorded action gives the 'menu' value for Specified Distance or the key and unit of the distance value (checked BlendSp, AI_PS_Library and public .aia files on GitHub). Record Object > Blend > Blend Options with this spacing in Illustrator to obtain them; no object-model member exposes it.

features.name: Specified Steps
features.summary: Exact number of intermediate steps.

automation.notes: Set through a loaded action: event ai_plugin_liveblend with spacing enum (key 'menu') value 5 and the step count as integer parameter key 'step', run by app.loadAction then app.doScript with a blend selected. No object-model member exposes steps.

features.name: Blend Options
features.summary: Sets blend spacing and orientation.

features.name: Blend panel
features.summary: Panel with blend creation, steps, easing, colour acceleration, spine and expand controls.

automation.notes: Inferred: no member in any held object-model version, no command id in commands.json and no community script opens or drives the Blend panel. Its make, release and expand functions are reached separately through the Path Blend menu commands, and steps and orientation through a loaded action.

features.name: Control color acceleration
features.summary: Changes how quickly colour shifts across the blend.

automation.notes: Inferred: no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script sets colour acceleration; it is set only in the Blend panel.

features.name: Ease the blend steps
features.summary: Bunches steps toward one end of the blend instead of spacing them evenly.

automation.notes: Inferred: no member in any held object-model version, no command id and no community script sets blend step easing; it is set only in the Blend panel.

features.name: Release
features.summary: Removes the blend and restores the original objects.

features.name: Replace Spine
features.summary: Uses a selected path as the blend's new spine.

features.name: Reverse Front to Back
features.summary: Reverses the stacking order of the blend steps.

features.name: Reverse Spine
features.summary: Reverses the order of objects along the spine.

features.name: Create text designs with blend objects
features.summary: Using blends on type for 3D-like lettering.

automation.notes: Steps: create the text, convert it to outlines, select two copies and run Path Blend Make; set steps and orientation by playing a loaded ai_plugin_liveblend action. Positioning the copies is ordinary PageItem work.

features.name: Blend Tool
features.summary: Creates a blend by clicking the objects to blend between.

automation.notes: Tool id "Adobe Blend Tool" (AiCommandPalette tool list) activates the tool; clicking objects with it stays interactive. The same result on a selection comes from the menu command Path Blend Make.

features.name: Apply Last Effect

features.name: Ellipse

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

features.name: Rounded Rectangle
features.summary: Draws the object's appearance as a rounded rectangle.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

features.name: Crop Marks
features.summary: Adds crop marks around the object as a live effect.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

features.name: Document Raster Effects Settings
features.summary: Sets the resolution and options used by every raster effect in the document.

features.name: Drop Shadow
features.summary: Adds an offset, blurred shadow behind the object.

automation.notes: PageItem.applyEffect applies it as a live effect, without a dialog, from LiveEffect XML "Adobe Drop Shadow" with I blnd (1 multiply), R opac (0-1), R horz and R vert (offsets in points), R blur (points), B usePSLBlur, I csrc 1 with R dark (darkness in percent), and an sclr Fill entry for the colour. Adobe does not document the XML; these parameters are the ones the cited published scripts use. The menu command remains an alternative but opens the dialog and needs a selection. Object > Expand Appearance (command "expandStyle") makes the result permanent.

features.name: Blur
features.summary: Softness of the shadow edge.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Drop Shadow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; this option is the Dict entry 'R blur'. Parameter names come from community scripts, not Adobe documentation; applying adds a new effect rather than editing an existing one.

features.name: Color
features.summary: Colour of the shadow.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Drop Shadow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; this option is the Dict entry 'I csrc' (colour source) with an Entry named 'sclr' holding a Fill colour. Parameter names come from community scripts, not Adobe documentation; applying adds a new effect rather than editing an existing one.

features.name: Darkness
features.summary: Percentage of black mixed into the object's colour for the shadow.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Drop Shadow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; this option is the Dict entry 'R dark', used when the colour source is darkness. Parameter names come from community scripts, not Adobe documentation; applying adds a new effect rather than editing an existing one.

features.name: Mode
features.summary: Blending mode of the shadow.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Drop Shadow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; this option is the Dict entry 'I blnd' (blend mode as an integer; the mapping of numbers to modes is not documented). Parameter names come from community scripts, not Adobe documentation; applying adds a new effect rather than editing an existing one.

features.name: Opacity
features.summary: Opacity of the shadow.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Drop Shadow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; this option is the Dict entry 'R opac' (0 to 1). Parameter names come from community scripts, not Adobe documentation; applying adds a new effect rather than editing an existing one.

features.name: X Offset
features.summary: Horizontal offset of the shadow.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Drop Shadow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; this option is the Dict entry 'R horz'. Parameter names come from community scripts, not Adobe documentation; applying adds a new effect rather than editing an existing one.

features.name: Y Offset
features.summary: Vertical offset of the shadow.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Drop Shadow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; this option is the Dict entry 'R vert'. Parameter names come from community scripts, not Adobe documentation; applying adds a new effect rather than editing an existing one.

features.name: Effect Gallery
features.summary: Opens the Effect Gallery to preview and stack Photoshop-style raster effects.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources. Its only command, "Live PSAdapter_plugin_GEfc" (Effect > Effect Gallery...), opens the modal Effect Gallery dialog. The effects it stacks are Photoshop filters whose LiveEffect parameters are stored as an ascii85-encoded binary blob with a dataSize, which no published script decodes or builds, so PageItem.applyEffect cannot set them either.

features.name: Edit or remove effects
features.summary: Changing or deleting an effect from the Appearance panel.

automation.notes: No member lists, edits or deletes a single effect in the appearance stack. A script can only add effects (applyEffect), replace the whole appearance by applying a graphic style such as the document's first ([Default]) style with ArtStyle.applyTo, or bake it in with Expand Appearance. Only partly reachable. No object-model member lists, edits or deletes a single effect in an item's appearance stack. Scripts can add effects (PageItem.applyEffect, used by apply_effect, apply_svg_filter and pathfinder), bake them in with Expand Appearance ("expandStyle", their expand option), or replace the whole appearance by applying a graphic style. Editing or removing one effect is left to the Appearance panel.

features.name: Feather
features.summary: Softens the object's edges so they fade to transparent.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

features.name: Free Distort
features.summary: Distorts the object by dragging the four corners of its bounding box.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

features.name: Blur
features.summary: Spread of the glow.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Inner Glow" or "Adobe Outer Glow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; spread is 'R blur'. Names come from Adobe Community posts, not Adobe documentation.

features.name: Center
features.summary: Inner glow radiates from the centre.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Inner Glow" or "Adobe Outer Glow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; Inner Glow only: the Center or Edge choice is the integer 'gtyp'; which value means Center is not established. Names come from Adobe Community posts, not Adobe documentation.

features.name: Edge
features.summary: Inner glow radiates from the edges.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Inner Glow" or "Adobe Outer Glow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; Inner Glow only: the Center or Edge choice is the integer 'gtyp'; which value means Edge is not established. Names come from Adobe Community posts, not Adobe documentation.

features.name: Mode
features.summary: Blending mode of the glow.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Inner Glow" or "Adobe Outer Glow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; the blend mode is the Dict entry 'I blnd' (number-to-mode mapping not documented). Names come from Adobe Community posts, not Adobe documentation.

features.name: Opacity
features.summary: Opacity of the glow.

automation.notes: LiveEffect "Adobe Inner Glow" or "Adobe Outer Glow" applied with PageItem.applyEffect; opacity is 'R opac' (0 to 1). Names come from Adobe Community posts, not Adobe documentation.

features.name: Inner Glow
features.summary: Adds a soft glow inside the object's edges or from its centre.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

features.name: Last Effect
features.summary: Opens the dialog of the most recently used effect to apply it with new settings.

automation.notes: Its only command, "Adobe Last Effect" (Effect > Last Effect), opens the most recent effect's modal dialog to choose new settings. Reapplying with the same settings is "Adobe Apply Last Effect", which apply_last_effect runs; new settings are given to apply_effect directly instead.

features.name: Live effect
features.summary: A non-destructive modification attached to an object's appearance that can be edited or removed later.

automation.notes: applyEffect takes LiveEffect XML whose schema our sources do not document.

features.name: Offset Path
features.summary: Offsets the object's outline by a distance as a live effect.

automation.notes: PageItem.applyEffect applies it as a live effect, without a dialog, from LiveEffect XML "Adobe Offset Path" with R ofst (offset in points), I jntp (0 round, 1 bevel, 2 miter) and R mlim (miter limit). Adobe does not document the XML; these parameters are the ones the cited published scripts use. The menu command remains an alternative but opens the dialog and needs a selection. Object > Expand Appearance (command "expandStyle") makes the result permanent.

features.name: Outer Glow
features.summary: Adds a soft glow outside the object's edges.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

features.name: Outline Object
features.summary: Treats the object's outline (for example text) as a path for other effects.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

features.name: Outline Stroke
features.summary: Treats the stroke as a filled outline for other effects.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

features.name: Add
features.summary: Live version of Unite for grouped objects.

automation.notes: PageItem.applyEffect applies it as a live effect, without a dialog, from LiveEffect XML "Adobe Pathfinder" with I Command 0, plus R Precision, B RemovePoints and B ExtractUnpainted (Pathfinder Options), applied to a group of the objects. Adobe does not document the XML; these parameters are the ones the cited published scripts use. The menu command remains an alternative but opens the dialog and needs a selection. Object > Expand Appearance (command "expandStyle") makes the result permanent.

features.name: Crop
features.summary: Live version of Crop.

automation.notes: PageItem.applyEffect applies it as a live effect, without a dialog, from LiveEffect XML "Adobe Pathfinder" with I Command 9, plus R Precision, B RemovePoints and B ExtractUnpainted (Pathfinder Options), applied to a group of the objects. Adobe does not document the XML; these parameters are the ones the cited published scripts use. The menu command remains an alternative but opens the dialog and needs a selection. features.name: Divide
features.summary: Live version of Divide.

automation.notes: PageItem.applyEffect applies it as a live effect, without a dialog, from LiveEffect XML "Adobe Pathfinder" with I Command 5, plus R Precision, B RemovePoints and B ExtractUnpainted (Pathfinder Options), applied to a group of the objects. Adobe does not document the XML; these parameters are the ones the cited published scripts use. The menu command remains an alternative but opens the dialog and needs a selection. Object > Expand Appearance (command "expandStyle") makes the result permanent.

features.name: Exclude
features.summary: Live version of Exclude.

automation.notes: PageItem.applyEffect applies it as a live effect, without a dialog, from LiveEffect XML "Adobe Pathfinder" with I Command 2, plus R Precision, B RemovePoints and B ExtractUnpainted (Pathfinder Options), applied to a group of the objects. Adobe does not document the XML; these parameters are the ones the cited published scripts use. The menu command remains an alternative but opens the dialog and needs a selection. features.name: Hard Mix
features.summary: Combines colours of overlapping areas using the highest value of each component.

automation.notes: Applies as a live effect that stays editable in the Appearance panel. PageItem.applyEffect accepts a LiveEffect XML string, but the XML for this effect is not documented in our sources.

features.name: Add or remove objects from a clipping mask

features.name: Clip group

features.name: Clip (opacity mask)
features.summary: Makes the opacity mask also clip the artwork to its shape.

features.name: Clipping path
features.summary: The path in a clip group whose shape hides everything outside it.

features.name: Draw Inside
features.summary: Drawing mode that clips new artwork to the selected object, creating a clip group.

features.name: Hide parts of objects with clipping masks

features.name: Invert Mask

features.name: Make

automation.notes: Name, function key and colour are fields of the .aia file (/name, /keyIndex, /colorIndex in the cited script), set when the script writes the file before loading it; a loaded action cannot be changed. Claimed by load_actions for renaming only: the action's /name in a script-written .aia file is replaced before Application.loadAction. The function key and colour are the /keyIndex and /colorIndex fields, but no published source maps their values to keys or colours (scripts write 0; Illustrator's own saved files also use 7 for colour), so they are left as they are. A loaded action cannot be changed.

No member restores the default actions, and the panel's Reset Actions item asks for confirmation in a modal dialog and has no executeMenuCommand id. Application.unloadAction plus Application.loadAction replace the panel's sets only when given an .aia copy of the Default Actions set, and where Illustrator keeps that set is not documented. With such a saved copy, load_actions { replace: "all" } does the reset; without it nothing reaches the feature unattended.
